cname-not-alone.title: A CNAME must be alone on "{{subdomain}}"
cname-not-alone.detail: RFC 1034 sec. 3.6.2 forbids any other record next to a CNAME. Use an ALIAS instead if your provider supports it, it can live next to your other records.

dname-not-alone.title: A DNAME conflicts with the other records of "{{subdomain}}"
dname-not-alone.detail: A DNAME redirects a whole subtree, it cannot coexist with a CNAME at the same name (RFC 6672 sec. 2.4).

special-cname-not-alone.title: A CNAME must be alone on "{{subdomain}}"
special-cname-not-alone.detail: Another record already uses this service name. RFC 1034 sec. 3.6.2 forbids any other record next to a CNAME.

cname-at-apex.title: A CNAME cannot sit at the apex of "{{domain}}"
cname-at-apex.detail: The apex always carries the SOA and the NS records of the zone, so a CNAME can never be alone there. Use an ALIAS instead if your provider supports it.

empty-target.title: The alias has no target
empty-target.detail: Fill in the domain name this alias should point to.

invalid-target.title: Invalid target "{{target}}"
invalid-target.detail: An alias target must be a valid hostname, as defined by RFC 1035.

cname-loop.title: The alias points to itself ("{{target}}")
cname-loop.detail: A record aliasing its own name never resolves: pick a different target.

cname-chain.title: The target "{{target}}" is itself an alias
cname-chain.detail: Chaining aliases makes every lookup slower, and some resolvers refuse to follow the chain. Point this record straight at the final name.

dangling-target.title: The target "{{target}}" holds no record in this zone
dangling-target.detail: The alias points inside this zone, to a name that publishes nothing. Check the spelling, or add the records this name should carry.

Alias.name: Alias
Alias.description: Maps an alias to another (canonical) domain.
